skill.name: dependency-management-deps-audit
skill.description: Audit project dependencies for vulnerabilities, license conflicts, outdated packages, supply chain issues, and bundle size impact.
skill.summary: Find dependency security, license, update, and supply chain risks with practical remediation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most backtick and blocker alerts are false positives from Markdown or JavaScript examples. The real risks are outbound dependency metadata queries and automated remediation commands that can change project state.

remediation.issue: External package metadata requests can disclose package names and versions.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before querying public registries or Bundlephobia, and support offline or private-registry-only modes.

remediation.issue: Forceful automated updates may change dependency trees unexpectedly.
remediation.suggestion: Use dry-run mode first, remove --force from default examples, and require explicit confirmation before write operations.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use command substitution inside CI checks.
remediation.suggestion: Assign jq results to variables and validate numeric output before comparisons to reduce parsing errors.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is a JavaScript template literal used to build a Bundlephobia URL, not Ruby or shell execution. No shell interpreter is invoked.
The backticks format a JavaScript string for a size value. They do not execute a command or evaluate untrusted code.

The backticks create a JavaScript issue title string in a GitHub Actions example. No external command is executed by this expression.
The command substitution reads a local npm audit report with jq in a CI example. It is controlled workflow logic, not arbitrary command execution.
The substitution only prints a count from a local audit file. It has no user-controlled command path or injection target in this context.
The playbook provides a Bash remediation script that can run package manager and git commands if copied. This is legitimate for the skill, but it changes project state.
The code performs an outbound fetch for dependency size analysis. This can disclose package names and versions to an external service.
The word axios appears in a list of common package names for typosquatting checks. It is not imported or used as an HTTP client here.
The sample uses requests.post to query the npm audit API. This is expected, but it sends dependency names and versions to a network service.
The URL points to the npm security advisories API used for vulnerability checks. It is legitimate, but it is an external endpoint receiving dependency metadata.
The URL points to the PyPI package API. It supports the audit workflow but may reveal queried package names to a public service.
The URL points to the RubyGems package API. It is expected for dependency checks but still performs external metadata lookup.
The URL points to the Sonatype OSS Index component report API. It is a legitimate vulnerability source but requires outbound dependency metadata queries.
The sample posts dependency data to the npm security advisories endpoint. This is useful for scanning but exposes package metadata outside the local project.
The Bundlephobia URL is used for package size analysis. Querying it can disclose package names and versions to a third-party service.
The flagged line is a Python for loop over vulnerability records. It does not create hard links or perform filesystem mutation.
The flagged text is a pull request checklist item saying all tests pass. It contains no network scanning or reconnaissance behavior.
The backticks mark a Markdown file path. They are not Ruby backticks and do not trigger command execution.
The backticks mark a Markdown resource path. This is documentation formatting, not executable code.

content.value_statement: Dependency drift creates security, license, and maintenance risk across modern projects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured audits and remediation plans.
actual_capabilities: Inventories direct and transitive dependencies across common package managers.
Checks dependencies against vulnerability advisory sources and prioritizes severe issues.
Reviews license compatibility and highlights unknown or restrictive licenses.
Ranks outdated packages by security impact, release age, and update effort.
Flags supply chain risks such as typosquatting and recent maintainer changes.
Drafts remediation plans, pull request notes, and monitoring workflow guidance.
limitations: Requires access to dependency manifests, lockfiles, or package metadata.
May need network access for current advisory and registry data.
Cannot prove runtime exploitability without project-specific validation.
Automated upgrade suggestions still require tests and human review.

use_cases.title: Audit Before Release
use_cases.description: Review dependencies before a production release and prioritize fixes that block shipment.

use_cases.title: Review License Exposure
use_cases.description: Identify incompatible, unknown, or restrictive dependency licenses before legal approval.

use_cases.title: Maintain Security Monitoring
use_cases.description: Design recurring dependency scans and alerts for repository changes and scheduled checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project for dependency vulnerabilities. Identify package managers, run safe read-only checks, and summarize critical fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Check License Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review dependency licenses for this repository. Flag incompatible, unknown, or restrictive licenses and suggest safe replacement options.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized dependency update plan. Include risk, upgrade target, testing scope, rollback notes, and owner-ready tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Build Continuous Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dependency security workflow for this project. Include scheduled scans, failure criteria, private package safeguards, and alert routing.

output_examples.input: Audit a Node.js service with package manifests and a lockfile.
output: Reports critical and high dependency vulnerabilities first.
Recommends patched versions and notes likely breaking changes.
Lists tests to run before merging the updates.

output_examples.input: Review a mixed Python and JavaScript project for license issues.
output: Flags GPL, AGPL, proprietary, and unknown licenses for review.
Suggests replacement research for high-risk packages.

output_examples.input: Prepare dependency monitoring for a repository.
output: Defines scheduled scans and manifest-triggered checks.
Sets failure rules for severe vulnerabilities.
Adds alert routing and review checklist guidance.

best_practices: Start with read-only scans before changing dependency files.
Separate security patches from major upgrades when possible.
Validate every update with tests, lockfile review, and rollback notes.
anti_patterns: Running forceful package updates without reviewing generated changes.
Ignoring private package disclosure when using public registry APIs.
Treating vulnerability counts as proof of exploitability without context.

faq.question: Does this skill update dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose commands and scripts, but users should approve and review changes before execution.

faq.question: Which ecosystems are covered?
faq.answer: The playbook references npm, Python, Ruby, Maven, Go, Rust, PHP, and .NET dependency files.

faq.question: Can it check licenses?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews license compatibility, restrictive licenses, unknown licenses, and compliance risks.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Some checks use external advisory, registry, and package size services for current data.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for security review?
faq.answer: No. It supports triage and planning, but teams must validate exploitability and business impact.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it in a repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It is structured for repository audits when manifests and lockfiles are available.
